 Broncos’ Jaylen Waddle injured chest on ‘dumb’ Sean Payton play call: ‘It was awful’ 
 Waddle grabbed at his left chest area after recovering a fumble on a botched reverse

 Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (17) leaves the field after an injury during the second half of an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals in Glendale, Ariz., Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin) 
 By Parker Gabriel | pgabriel@denverpost.com | The Denver Post PUBLISHED: October 25, 2026 at 5:24 PM MDT | UPDATED: October 25, 2026 at 7:00 PM MDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... GLENDALE, Ariz — Sean Payton took matters into his own hands.
 Five minutes into his postgame news conference after a 30-16 win over Arizona , the Broncos head coach called his own number — and criticized himself in the process.
 “Why hasn’t anyone asked me about the dumb reverse call?” Payton wondered, getting more animated as he talked. “I’m going to answer. Everyone ask the question.
 “It was awful, alright, I’m sorry.”
 Payton had a historical comparison, too.
 “If you look it up, in 2008 in a similar situation, even a more radical reverse,” he said. “Fumbled. Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play.”
 Arizona didn’t come back and beat the Broncos, of course, but the play did lose 11 yards. Denver retained possession because top wide receiver Jaylen Waddle fell on the ball.
 The problem this time around? Waddle also got hurt on the play .
 It came with 4:51 left in regulation and Denver leading by two touchdowns.
 Payton, who felt he and the offensive staff had put together a terrific game plan against Arizona’s zone-blitzing defense, dialed up a reverse for his top receiver. The ball got fumbled, though, and Waddle jumped on it.
 When he rolled over, Waddle grabbed his left chest and shoulder area with his right hand and didn’t get up until trainers came out to check on him. The team ultimately called it a chest injury.
 After stopping in the medical tent for evaluation, Waddle left the game and headed back to the locker room.

 Broncos-Cardinals report card: Explosive plays galore in Denver’s convincing win 
 Before the injury, Waddle had four catches for 48 yards.
 Waddle was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday with what was listed as a chest injury, then was a full participant Friday and was cleared to play against the Cardinals.
 The immediate severity of the injury was not known and Payton did not divulge any update.
 Waddle injured his ankle earlier in the season but has played in all seven games for the Broncos. He’s now got 276 yards and a touchdown through seven games, putting him on pace for a career-low 670 yards for the season.
 The Broncos landed Waddle in March, trading a first-round pick and more to Miami to acquire him.
 Zach Allen ‘fine’ after hamstring scare
 All-Pro defensive tackle Zach Allen left the game late with a right hamstring issue but appears to have avoided a serious injury.
 “I’ll be fine,” Allen said flatly after the game.
 Allen, a former Cardinal, spoke at the podium, which players typically don’t do if they sustain an injury during the game.
 Allen finished a play on Arizona’s final drive, then grabbed his right hamstring and sat down. Trainers came out to look at him and he eventually walked off gingerly on his own.
 Allen did not go to the medical tent. He watched the final plays on the sideline with his helmet off.
 Pat Surtain II misses third game with ankle injury
 Star cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) did not play in Denver’s win over the Cardinals.
 That development wasn’t a huge surprise after Surtain was listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report.
 Since he was first injured against San Francisco in early October, the Broncos have been aiming for a Week 8 return for Surtain. That’s next weekend against Kansas City.
 Surtain traveled to the desert with the team and watched in street clothes from the sideline.
 Sai’Vion Jones into the sack ledger
 Denver second-year defensive lineman Sai’Vion Jones has carved out a nice role for himself as a sophomore in the NFL.
 He’s mostly been asked to play run downs and do dirty work, but Sunday he put himself in the book with his first career sack.
 Jones, a 2025 third-round pick out of LSU, sacked Arizona’s Jacoby Brissett early in the fourth quarter. It helped the Broncos defense get to its feet, too, after a 27-yard completion to star tight end Trey McBride (10 catches, 111 yards, TD). Denver followed up Jones’ sack by forcing a turnover on downs.
